CITY OF PASADENA
  City Council Minutes
  March 15, 2021-4:30 P.M.
  City Hall Council Chamber

  SPECIAL MEETING
  The virtual meeting was convened pursuant to Executive Order N-29-20 issued by
  Governor Gavin Newsom on March 17, 2020, and was held solely by
  videoconference/teleconference

OPENING:  Mayor Gordo called the special meeting to order at 4:37 p.m. The
  pledge of allegiance was led by Councilmember Rivas.

ROLL CALL:  Mayor Victor M. Gordo
 Councilmembers:  Vice Mayor Andy Wilson
  Councilmember Tyron Hampton
  Councilmember John J. Kennedy
  Councilmember Steve Madison
  Councilmember Gene Masuda
  Councilmember Jessica Rivas
  Councilmember Felicia Williams

  Staff:  City Manager Steve Mermell
  City Attorney/City Prosecutor Michele Beal Bagneris
  City Clerk Mark Jomsky

CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Gordo requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory
  of those that have suffered due to death and illness caused by
  COVID-19 in Pasadena, the nation, and around the world.

  Mayor Gordo announced that the deadline to submit an application
  for the Community Police Oversight Commission is today by 5:00
  p.m., and provided information on the next steps, which include
  reviewing applications, as well as the selection process. In addition,
  he announced that Councilmember Rivas has been appointed to
  the Municipal Services Committee and the Economic Development
  and Technology Committee.

SPECIAL ITEM  VACCINATIONS AND RE-OPENING - DR. YING-YING GOH,
  PUBLIC HEALTH OFFICER

  Steve Mermell, City Manager, provided introductory comments, and
  Dr. Ying-Ying Goh, Public Health Officer, reported that COVID-19
  cases have decreased significantly over the past few weeks, and
  spoke on the importance for the public to continue to wear masks,
  wash hands, and watch their distance from each other (the three
  "W's"). Dr. Goh provided an update on COVID-19 positive cases in
  Pasadena; the tracking of COVID-19 virus variances; information
  on the State's travel advisory; encouraged individuals who are
  eligible for the COVID-19 vaccine to sign up for the vaccination; the
  Health Officer order to allow the opening and expansion of multiple

Council Minutes  03/15/2021
   businesses and business sector activities; update on vaccinated
  Pasadena residents, and large-scale vaccination clinics; and the
  progress of reopening of schools in the City; and responded to
  questions.

  Councilmember Kennedy stated the following for the record , "Can
  you tell me why it is that it is taking so long to vaccinate
  Councilmembers?" In response, Dr. Goh reviewed the State
  vaccination requirements and stated that the State has determined
  that elected officials, such as Councilmembers, qualify for vaccine
  when government workers are added to the COVID-19 vaccination
  eligibility list.

  Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the importance of encouraging
  minorities to get the vaccine (noting the reluctance of some
  individuals to get vaccinated), and recommended that the Mayor
  and Councilmembers be publically vaccinated to help encourage
  those in the community that are reluctant to do so. He asked staff
  to provide information on the process/policy used by the City of
  Long Beach to vaccinate their Mayor and Councilmembers.

  Councilmember Madison asked staff to provide information on the
  percentage of City employees who are vaccinated and/or will be
  vaccinated when eligible to receive the COVID-19 vaccination; and
  spoke in favor of the City Council adopting a mandatory vaccination
  policy for City employees.

  Mayor Gordo echoed the request for data on the number of City
  employees that have been vaccinated, including percentage of the
  City's workforce that is eligible for the COVID-19 vaccination, how
  many have refused or indicated that they will not accept the vaccine,
  and report back to the City Council through the City Manager's
  weekly Newsletter.

  Councilmember Rivas also spoke in support of Councilmembers
  being provided the COVlD-19 vaccination.

  Councilmember Hampton requested that the next COVI D-19
  update include a written staff report prior to the City Council
  meeting. He spoke on the importance of reaching out to the Latinx
  community; and suggested staff contact the Pasadena Police
  Department's chaplain for recommendations on how best to reach
  that segment of the City's population. He also suggested that Health
  Department staff consider visiting the senior community door-to-
  door and vaccinate them in their homes. Councilmember Hampton
  expressed concerns with adopting a policy mandating that City
  employees be vaccinated, which he believes is not legal.

Council Minutes  2  03/1 5/2021
   Councilmember Kennedy spoke on the need to provide information
  regarding the availability of vaccines in English and Spanish,
  including articles in the Pasadena lnFocus newsletter, and by
  collaborating with the Pasadena Unified School District, Spanish
  speaking radio stations, newspaper organizations, and markets,
  and Pasadena City College to disseminate the information. He
  expressed concerns with the vaccine distribution at Planned
  Parenthood sites, as some members of the public may not feel
  comfortable going to those locations.

  Councilmember Williams stated that she is having difficulty
  scheduling an appointment for the COVID-19 vaccination through
  the "MY TURN" website; and advocated for the City's Public Health
  Department to continue to schedule vaccination appointments for
  City residents.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.

  FEDERAL COVID RELIEF PACKAGE - JULIE GUTIERREZ,
  ASSISTANT CITY MANAGER

  City Manager Mermell provided introductory comments, and Julie
  Gutierrez, Assistant City Manager, presented a PowerPoint
  presentation on the American Rescue Plan Act 2021, including
  information on State and local assistance, eligibility uses of funds ,
  and responded to questions.

  Vice Mayor Wilson asked staff to provide information on the total
  amount of the City's FEMA reimbursement request.

  Mayor Gordo expressed concerns that the funds associated with
  the American Rescue Plan Act 2021 will be provided directly to Los
  Angeles County and not the City of Pasadena, and requested that
  staff agenize the matter at the upcoming joint meeting of the City
  Council and Los Angeles County Supervisor Kathryn Barger. He
  spoke on the need to ensure that the funds the City receives are
  impactful to the City. He asked staff to determine how to replenish
  the City's reserves , which should be a priority.

  Councilmember Hampton advocated for use of the American
  Rescue Plan Act 2021 funds to update the City's fire stations,
  affordable housing, and park amenities. He spoke in favor of
  requesting Los Angeles County contribute funds to the City's
  Housing Department to assist with the City's housing needs.

  Councilmember Kennedy requested that once the American
  Rescue Plan Act 2021 funds are received that staff provide
  graphical data and a report on recommendations on how best to
  allocate the funds . He also reported that members of the Burbank-

Council Minutes  3  03/15/2021
   Glendale-Pasadena Airport Authority have stated that they will not
  be providing employee raises.

  Councilmember Madison clarified that the Airport Authority will not
  be providing raises for only those employees who are not
  represented by bargaining groups. He expressed concerns with the
  "strings attached" to the Rescue Plan Act 2021 funds; and stated
  that the funds are for COVI D-19 relief and not infrastructure.

  Mayor Gordo spoke on the need for staff to collect past due utility
  charges from common area expenditures of large apartments and
  condominium building operators.

  City Manager Mermell responded that staff, including the City
  Attorney's Office, are determining the best options to collect past
  due funds from those Water and Power customers.

  Vice Mayor Wilson requested that staff interface with the Small
  Business Administration (SBA), and Pasadena Chamber of
  Commerce on the Rescue Plan Act 2021 funds to determine what
  amounts will be allocated towards restaurant revitalization.

  Mayor Gordo stated that he will write a letter to the local SBA on
  behalf of the City Council asking for information on how the Rescue
  Plan Act 2021 funds will be allocated to restaurant revitalization and
  how the funds will be expended.

  City Clerk Jomsky reported that Jill Shook, representing Missions
  Door, submitted a letter advocating for the funds to be used for
  additional affordable housing in the City, which was distributed to
  the City Council, posted on-line, and made part of the public record.

  In addition, he read aloud comments advocating for additional relief
  to local businesses, housing for homeless individuals and
  affordable housing; and providing comments/suggestions from the
  following individuals:

  Paul Little, Pasadena Chamber of Commerce
  Sonja K. Berndt, Pasadena resident
  Donna Sider, Pasadena resident
  Anthony Manousos, Pasadena resident
  Jill Shook, Pasadena resident
  Teresa Eilers, Pasadena resident
  Cynthia Kirby, Pasadena resident

  Mayor Gordo asked staff to provide information on the eligibility of
  stimulus funds for the Pasadena Unified School District, private
  schools in the City, and Pasadena City College, and determine if
  there are projects (i.e. internet access projects) that may be
  coordinated with the City.

Council Minutes  4  03/15/2021
   Councilmember Kennedy spoke on recent violence in the City and
  asked staff to provide information on any plans that are being
  considered to address such violence taking place in the City.

  In response, Mayor Gordo stated that he has requested that the
  City Manager and Chief Perez provide an update at the
  Wednesday, March 17, 2021, Public Safety Committee meeting
  and provide their best thinking to combat recent violence.

  Following discussion, by consensus of the City Council, and on
  order of the Mayor, the information was received and filed.
